function: export async function runDesktop(page, { url, out, record })

arguments.page: Existing caller-owned Puppeteer Page; use a fresh isolated context for reproducibility.
arguments.url: Live HTTP(S) app URL; welcome=0 is added/replaced while preserving other query parameters.
arguments.out: Screenshot directory, created recursively when absent.
arguments.record: Caller-owned array; appended assertion entries have id, pass, detail, data, startedUtc, finishedUtc, utc, and viewport.

returns: Promise resolving to pass, UTC timing, viewport, query, saved sceneName, scene details, screenshot paths, and camera samples. Failure is recorded then rethrown.
checks: 1440x900 UI readiness and untouched baseline screenshot
Exact request typed using keyboard and submitted with Enter
Visible composer Play and scene name input
Read-only lastScene geographic anchor near 25.07864, 55.13525 (0.01-degree per-axis tolerance)
At least two keyframes and geographic=true
Actual name entry and save-button click; saved summary, feedback and selector option
Actual playback PLAY click; live clock advancement and camera movement
Actual PAUSE click; paused state and stable clock/camera
Actual NEXT and PREV clicks; selection changes, return to original shot, actual camera motion
screenshots: failure-<step> on error when page remains available
mutationPolicy: Only page navigation/viewport and native mouse/keyboard events. All evaluate/waitForFunction callbacks are read-only. No internal state injection, network mocks, overlay removal, rendering changes, or DOM input assignment.
limitations: No browser or deployed preview was available/requested for this implementation task; runtime pass is not claimed.
Coordinator/Agent20 must supply and clean up the browser/page and enforce a global wall-clock timeout.
Requires live composer/geocoder integration, scene library save wiring, and the existing debug read handles/selectors.
Uses finite per-step waits and bounded real-mouse scrolling; covered controls intentionally fail rather than bypass overlays.
NEXT/PREV settlement allows 2.8 seconds for the existing 2.2-second camera flight; materially different timing may require coordinator adjustment.
Saved-state checks prove UI save completion and selector presence, not persistence after reload.
No live network responses or screenshot contents were asserted during implementation.
